headline: The two most extreme phones ever, with displays that push boundaries
summary: These phones feature displays that stretch to the absolute edge, offering an immersive viewing experience unlike any other.
details: The latest smartphone designs are pushing the limits of what's possible with display technology. Two new phones showcase extreme edge-to-edge screens that create a truly immersive visual experience.

One device features a display that curves dramatically around the sides, minimizing bezels to near invisibility. This design choice aims to maximize screen real estate for content consumption and gaming.
The other phone boasts a nearly bezel-less flat display that extends right to the very edges of the chassis. This minimalist approach offers a clean aesthetic and an uninterrupted viewing surface.

While the exact models and their specifications are not detailed, the emphasis is on the extreme nature of their displays. These designs represent the cutting edge of smartphone screen innovation, prioritizing visual immersion above all else.

headline: Claude API multi-agent loop explained without frameworks
summary: Understand the core agent loop when Claude uses tools, directly from the engineer who built production systems.
details: Most Claude API tutorials show a single tool call, and many frameworks hide the agent loop behind abstractions. This post breaks down exactly what happens between Claude requesting a tool and finishing its response.

When using tools with Claude, a single API call isn't always enough. The agent loop involves Claude deciding to call a tool, you executing it, and then sending the result back. Claude might then call another tool or provide a final answer.

This implementation is designed for clarity and modification. The visible loop allows developers to add logging, approval gates, retry logic, or conditional execution precisely where needed, offering more control than abstracted frameworks.

The author used this pattern as the foundation for Cluster OS Jarvis, a production multi-agent framework. This post presents a simplified, standalone version of that loop for developers wanting to understand the underlying mechanics before adding abstractions.
